settings.name_in_paper: Feature-based bilateral trade, two-bit feedback, strong budget balance, deterministic valuations
unmapped: Bilateral trade: learner posts price to seller and buyer; reward is gain from trade 1{s_t<=p}1{q<=b_t}(b_t-s_t)
Strong budget balance: p_t = q_t each round
Valuations linear in context: s_t = x_t^T theta^s, b_t = x_t^T theta^b with unknown theta^s, theta^b
settings.definition_quote: s_t = x_t^{\top}\theta^s\quad\textnormal{ and }\quad b_t=x_t^\top\theta^b ... There exist $A,B\ge 0$ such that $\max(\Vert \theta^s\Vert, \Vert \theta^b\Vert) \leq A$, and $\Vert x_t\Vert \leq B$.

settings.name_in_paper: Feature-based bilateral trade, two-bit feedback, strong budget balance, noisy valuations
unmapped: Bilateral trade with gain-from-trade reward; two-bit feedback; strong budget balance p_t = q_t
Valuations x_t^T theta + i.i.d. centered noise independent of context, noise support [-C,C] and densities bounded by L
The learner knows the noise support bound C (through P = C + AB) and the density bound L
Contexts chosen by an oblivious adversary; pseudo-regret against best context-dependent price
settings.definition_quote: b_t = x_t^{\top}\theta^b + \xi_t^b \quad \text{ and }\quad s_t = x_t^{\top}\theta^s + \xi_t^s, where $\xi_t^b$ and $\xi_t^s$ are i.i.d.~centered noise terms independent from the context ... Both $\xi_t^s$ and $\xi_t^b$ have bounded support in $[-C,C]$, and have densities bounded by $L$.

settings.name_in_paper: Feature-based bilateral trade, one-bit feedback, global budget balance
unmapped: One-bit feedback: only whether trade happened 1{s_t<=p_t}1{q_t<=b_t}
Global budget balance: total profit sum_t (q_t-p_t)1{trade} >= 0 over the horizon
Learner knows the market-activity parameter alpha (used in the budget) and price range P
Generic reduction from any two-bit explore-or-commit algorithm
settings.definition_quote: the learning algorithm is global budget balanced if the following inequality holds: $\sum_{t=1}^T\prof(p_t,q_t)\ge 0$. ... One-bit feedback: the learner only observes whether the trade happened or not

algorithms.name: One-bit global-budget-balance reduction from two-bit EOC algorithm

source.label: thm:no_noise_2_bits
source.quote: Assume that the seller's and buyer's valuations follow \Cref{eq:2bit_no_noise}. Under \Cref{ass:bounded_context}, \Cref{alg:EPBT} with $\epsilon = ABd^2/T$ has regret bounded by $R_T \leq 10ABd^2\log\left(20(d+1)Td^{-2}\right)$.

results.notes: Paper's A mapped to S, B to L_feat. Deterministic algorithm and valuations, so regret is deterministic; worst-case over parameters and contexts. Quantity labeled unspecified/probability nominally expectation.

conditions: Assumptions 1 and 2: bounded parameters and contexts; noise support [-C,C] with densities bounded by L

source.label: thm:etc
source.quote: Set $\epsilon = (\log(T)/T)^{1/4}$, ... Then, under Assumptions \ref{ass:bounded_context} and \ref{ass:bounded_densities}, there exist a constant $\widetilde T$ such that, if $T\geq \widetilde T$, $R_T \leq  \widetilde O( T^{\nicefrac{3}{4}})$ with probability at least $1-T^{-1}$.

results.notes: Pseudo-regret (expected GFT) bound holding with probability 1-1/T over the learner's randomness/feedback.

conditions: Assumptions 1 and 2: bounded parameters and contexts; noise support [-C,C] with densities bounded by L

source.label: thm:noise_2_bits
source.quote: Assume that the valuations of the buyer and the seller follow the noisy linear model in Equation \eqref{eq:2bit_noise}. Let $\epsilon = (d^2\log(T)^2/T)^{\nicefrac{1}{3}}$, ... Then, under Assumptions \ref{ass:bounded_context} and \ref{ass:bounded_densities}, with probability at least $1 - 1/T$, \Cref{alg:SBLBT} has a regret bounded by $R_T \leq \widetilde O(T^{\nicefrac{2}{3}})$.

results.notes: Proof gives R_T <= C'(d log(T) T)^{2/3} with C' depending on A,B,C,L (with probability 1-20T^{-2/3} in the appendix, inconsistent with statement). Remark 1 says minimax optimal up to logs and d via CesaBianchi et al. lower bound.

symbols.T_e: number of exploration rounds of the two-bit algorithm (w.p. >= 1-1/T)
symbols.R_2: commit-phase regret of the two-bit algorithm

conditions: Assumption 3 (active market): for each t' >= log T, sum_{t<=t'}(b_t - s_t) >= alpha_mkt t'
given a two-bit explore-or-commit strong-budget-balanced algorithm with at most T_e exploration rounds w.p. 1-1/T
tuning: budget = max{2048 P^4 alpha_mkt^-2 log^3 T, 2 P T_e}

source.label: thm: one bit regret
source.quote: Under \Cref{assumption:active market}, given the two-bit algorithm $\algA$, the corresponding one-bit learning algorithm satisfies global budget balance and, with probability at least $1-1/T$, has regret \[\regone\le  O(\te)\cdot \textnormal{polylog}(T) +\regtwo.\]

results.notes: O(T_e)*polylog(T) recorded as O_tilde. Instantiations in text: Õ(T^{3/4}) for noisy setting with EOC-BT, polylog(T) for noiseless; Remark 2 gives Õ(T^{3/4}) (deterministic) and Õ(T^{7/8}) (noisy) without Assumption 3. These informal statements not recorded separately.
